note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English; the original work has it as Eutermes westraliensis, and the synonymy cites 1921 (description of the soldier and worker) and 1925 (description of the alate). The first sentence of Affinities in the original reads "The winged adult is distinguished from E. ___ inter alia, by its larger size…", with the name of the allied species missing in the OCR, so the diagnostic characters list only the differences from E. hastilis and E. tumuli and do not supply the missing name. OCR misreadings: 'Pigs.'/'Pig.' = 'Figs.'/'Fig.', 'Pont an el le' = 'Fontanelle', 'prenotum' = 'pronotum', 'G-osnells' = 'Gosnells', 'ceils' = 'cells', 'small!r' = 'smaller', and 'mummy brown' and 'sepia' are colour names of the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is a small, very dark species with dark brown wings: head and thorax almost black, antennae 16-segmented with segment 3 the shortest of the whole antenna, pronotum far narrower than the head. Compared with E. hastilis it is smaller with darker wings; compared with E. tumuli it is smaller with a much smaller pronotum. The soldier is a large species, easily distinguished from the others by the long, curved nasus as long as the head capsule, with antennae of 14 or 15 segments and very long, slender legs. The worker has a dark brown head and antennae of 16 or 17 segments.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small, very dark species with dark brown wings. Head and thorax almost black; first antennal segment, abdomen and legs slightly paler; postclypeus slightly paler than the legs. Head hairless, with only sparse small hairs; hemispherical behind the compound eyes, frons flat. Fontanelle small, usually indistinct, about as long as the ocellus, widened in front. Compound eyes rather small and projecting. Ocelli small, projecting, far from the compound eyes. Postclypeus small, less than half as long as wide, strongly convex, hairless. Antennae 16-segmented; segment 3 short and narrow, the shortest of the whole antenna; segment 4 wider than segment 3 and more spherical; segment 5 longer and wider than segments 4 and 6. Second mandibular tooth about as large as the first. Pronotum far narrower than the head, with sparse short yellow hairs, anterior margin nearly straight, anterolateral angles rounded, sides narrowed to the slightly wavy posterior margin. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum wide and shallowly concave. Measurements: length with wings 11.50—12.00 mm; length without wings 5.50—6.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.42—1.50 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.77—0.88 mm; head width 1.20—1.24 mm; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.28 mm; ocellus length 0.11 mm; pronotum length 0.55—0.62 mm; pronotum width 0.91—0.95 mm; fore wing length 9.00—9.50 mm; fore wing width 2.60—2.75 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A large species, easily distinguished from the others by the long, curved nasus. Head almost hairless, very dark brown, the nasus slightly darker than the posterior part of the head; antennae, thorax, femora and abdominal tergites snuff brown. Head long and narrow, narrowed towards the antennal insertions; nasus as long as the head capsule, stout, arched above. Antennae long and slender, 14 or 15-segmented; segment 1 more than twice as long as segment 2; segment 2 usually the shortest of the whole antenna, occasionally as long as segment 3; segments 3 and 4 usually equal, shorter than segment 5, occasionally longer than segment 5; the following segments long and narrow. Mandibles with or without a short pointed tooth, sometimes with a pointed tooth on one side only. Legs very long and slender. Measurements: body length 4.25—5.25 mm; head length (to apex of nasus) 1.83—1.94 mm; head width 0.93—0.99 mm; pronotum width 0.55—0.58 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head dark brown, with a clear median and transverse suture. Antennae long and slender, 16 or 17-segmented; segment 3 very short; segment 5 far longer than segments 4 and 6. Postclypeus about half as long as wide. Measurements: body length 5.50 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.90—2.12 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.13—1.21 mm; head width 1.58—1.65 mm; pronotum width 0.80 mm.
